issues.description: Method name mismatch for StockIngredient quantity accessor: The template class de.tum.cit.ase.StockIngredient defines a method named retrieveQuantity() that returns the ingredient quantity, whereas the template Stock class (and the example code in Main) call getQuantity(). The solution repository provides getQuantity(). This naming inconsistency (retrieveQuantity vs getQuantity) prevents the template code from compiling and blocks students from using the provided Stock and Main examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a public int getQuantity() method to the template StockIngredient class (or rename retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity()) so that its API matches the calls in Stock and Main. For example: public int getQuantity() { return this.quantity; } You may keep retrieveQuantity() as an alias if desired, but ensure getQuantity() exists to match the solution and the example usages.

issues.description: Getter naming mismatch for the StockIngredient.quantity concept: the problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" (expects standard getter names like getQuantity()). In the template repository, the StockIngredient class defines retrieveQuantity() (template: StockIngredient.retrieveQuantity()) while other code and the reference solution use getQuantity() (template: Stock.findStockIngredient()/add()/take() call getQuantity(); solution: StockIngredient.getQuantity()). This inconsistency prevents a straightforward mapping from the requirement to the template, and in the template the Stock class calls getQuantity() which does not exist, causing compilation errors and blocking students.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter name for the quantity field consistent across artifacts. Rename the template's StockIngredient.retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity(), or add a public getQuantity() that delegates to retrieveQuantity(). Ensure the Stock class in the template calls getQuantity(). This aligns the template with the problem expectation and the solution and removes the compile-time confusion.
